A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PATHEVAL study and contain 19 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables, figures and embedded links support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, encoder-probing and fine-tuning results in Tables 1–5, plus supplementary experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original VLM evaluations, encoder-probing, fine-tuning and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: Benchmark generation, VLM prompting and fine-tuning, and the encoder-discrimination procedure in Sections 3–5 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same fifteen scenarios, four obstacle arrangements, 2D/3D representations and controlled perception datasets. Appendix A's scenario coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine VLMs and random baseline, and Table 4 retains the same six vision encoders. Comparator membership also matches within the supplementary experiments.

E3.justification: The 13,500/1,050 training/test split, input conditions, metrics, sample sizes and training budgets are unchanged, including the protocols in Appendix C.

E4.justification: The path-order and label-bias tests, descriptor-gap and segment-complexity analyses, encoder probing, scenario breakdowns, memorization experiments and failure examples are identical.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 specifies five repetitions per scenario in both versions. Repeated-run reporting is unchanged, with no confidence intervals, significance tests or seed information introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains GPT-4o's image-only accuracies of 0.665 for 2D and 0.624 for 3D.

T1.justification: The task formulation in Section 3.1, normalization in Section 3.5 and seven descriptor formulas in Appendix B are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about the perception bottleneck, limitations of end-to-end fine-tuning and need for task-specific encoder adaptation.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving visual ambiguity, label bias, segment complexity and misuse of commonsense remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D. No applicability boundaries or limitations are revised.

D1.justification: The page-1 code/data footnote is repaired: v1 encodes an internal link returning to page 1, whereas v2 encodes an external link to the intended PathEval repository. Prompts, hyperparameters and hardware documentation are unchanged. This establishes a navigation fix, not new repository contents or confirmed online availability.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 84 references and the positioning of PATHEVAL relative to planning, VLM perception and existing benchmarks are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 27 Nov 2024 to v2 dated 4 Mar 2025. Prose, authorship, terminology, headings and document organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–13 retain identical graphics, captions, structure and placement. Rendered pages differ only in the version/date stamp noted under P1.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs the code/data hyperlink that previously returned readers to page 1, allowing navigation to the intended external repository. This modestly improves access to the stated resources; the scientific arguments, experimental evidence and appendix documentation remain unchanged.
